    # gh-1471: the display name cannot read ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }} — the
    # env context is not available in job names (run 37580748776 died at
    # workflow startup on that) — but needs outputs ARE (same pattern as
    # bench-harbor.yml), so every shard names the provider+model: glm and
    # kimi runs never blend in the run history.
    name: fa on terminal-bench · ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }}
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Worst case per shard is LPT-packed to 340 min (job cap − 15 min
    # headroom, issue #1392); 355 min covers it under the 6 h runner cap.
    # --n-concurrent 1 keeps the math sequential-predictable and the total
    # concurrent LLM load at max-parallel x 1 (z.ai rate limits).
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Issue #1392 ShardStagger: split 8, run at most `max-concurrent`
      # (default 2) at once — GHA queues the rest and starts each the
      # moment a slot frees. This IS the concurrency experiment's
      # semaphore; no runner-side coordination.
      max-parallel: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.max-concurrent) }}
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - run: pip install terminal-bench

      # Populate tb's dataset cache, then patch it in place (tb run reuses a
      # non-empty cache without overwriting): debian:-based task images
      # cannot `apt-get update` during docker compose build since Debian
      # archived bullseye (issue #142).
      - name: Download & patch dataset
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR: ${{ inputs.test-timeout-floor }}
        run: |
          tb datasets download -d "$DATASET"
          python bench/terminal_bench/patch_dataset.py \
            "$HOME/.cache/terminal-bench/${DATASET%%==*}/${DATASET##*==}"
          # gh-1206: pad declared test budgets up to the floor so
          # slow-start verifier phases (jupyter, databases; judge phases
          # apt/pip-installing their own deps) stop dying as test_timeout
          # while the agent's work is already done. Empty/0 input = no
          # floor (declared budgets byte-for-byte).
          python bench/terminal_bench/patch_test_timeouts.py \
            "$HOME/.cache/terminal-bench/${DATASET%%==*}/${DATASET##*==}" \
            --floor "$TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR"

      - name: Run terminal-bench (fa agent)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/terminal_bench

          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. Both bench keys are mapped here;
          # the run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py
          # ships exactly that key into the container.

          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # dataset task dir names: no whitespace, safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # Issue #1392: the forensics layer is opt-in by env — this run IS
          # the instrumented experiment, so it opts in deliberately (the
          # adapter forwards these into the container base64-encoded via
          # _CONN_ENV_KEYS). ConnTrace gives every trial's bench_metrics.json
          # its per-request/watchdog events and the [fa-bench] live lines;
          # the payload snapshot is what StallSentinel's hang-*.json
          # captures (see FA_CONN_PAYLOAD_KEEP_AUTH — the snapshot redacts
          # auth unless that is set, which bench never does).
          FA_CONN_DEBUG: '1'
          FA_CONN_TRACE_FILE: /tmp/fa-conn-trace.jsonl
          FA_CONN_PAYLOAD_SNAPSHOT: /tmp/fa-conn-snapshot.json
          # The concurrency level lands in every trial's bench_metrics.json
          # (concurrency_level) and the report's per-level latency block.
          FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY: ${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}

          set -euo pipefail

          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"

"""Terminal-Bench adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Follows the AbstractInstalledAgent pattern (same as the claude-code agent):
a setup script installs fa inside the task container, and the agent runs as
`fa -p "<instruction>"` in the container's tmux session, so fa's bash/read/
write tools operate on the container filesystem.

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah + lib/),
                         extracted to /opt/fa by the setup script.
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122, see bench/fa_agent_timeout.py): when any
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER is set, perform_task takes over the outer
  agent deadline from the harness's flat wait_for: the agent runs under a
  progress-aware ladder (silent => die at the base cap as today; output
  flowing => deadline recedes up to the hard ceiling). With no knobs set
  this module delegates to the stock AbstractInstalledAgent.perform_task
  byte-for-byte (historical comparability, issue #1122 REG-1).

  Round 3 (issue #1392): when FA_STALL_GAP_SEC or
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC activates the progress-watch mode, the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch (progressing trials die
  only at the absolute ceiling; a >= stall-gap gap is a provable stall).
  Every trial also gets: live per-request lines as they happen
  (LiveProgress over the pane's FA_CONN events), a per-trial
  bench_metrics.json (latency p50/p95, watchdog fires, fresh-vs-reused),
  a hang-*.json forensics dump on a stall verdict BEFORE the kill lands
  (StallSentinel), and an export-guard.json row when the agent produced
  output but the session export came back empty (ExportGuard).

  gh-1430 — the ordering invariant this adapter operates under:

      fa's watchdog is the sole arbiter of stream death; the bench gap
      only catches pane/process death.

  fa errors a truly dead provider stream itself at
  providerStreamIdleTimeout (300s, lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart)
  and, since gh-1430, heartbeats `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` to the pane
  while its stream emits events the headless output mode does not render.
  The shipped stall gap (360s = watchdog + margin, bench/fa_agent_timeout.py)
  therefore fires only when the PANE went silent — process death or a
  wedged pane — never while fa itself considers the stream live. The REG
  in test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the gap >= watchdog against the Dart
  source and fails if either side drifts.

  Issue #1406 (never-again): the launch line itself carries the
  non-secret FA_CONN_* env into the tmux pane (`export …; env |
  grep FA_CONN > /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt;` prefix — pane env belongs to the
  shell/server history, not to the step env that typed a later command),
  the capture folds into agent-logs/fa-conn-env.txt as runtime proof,
  and the loud-empty guard fires (conn-guard.json + a ::warning::
  annotation) when a trial's bench_metrics.json has requests == []
  despite real usage tokens — an instrumentation outage is never silent.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;

arguments.newText:
- name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select(test("api.?key|^key$|token|secret"; "i"))] | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: acceptance criterion 2a not implemented — the `custom` provider escape hatch is missing**

The ticket's design **D1** makes the dispatch input a three-way choice — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default) / `kimi-for-coding` / **`custom`** — and acceptance criterion **2a** requires:

- `custom` selectable, with a free-text `provider-config` input carrying the provider JSON, passed through verbatim as `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` after validation;
- hard-fail validation: unparseable JSON, missing `baseUrl`/`model`, non-https `baseUrl`, any field named like `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` (case-insensitive) — the key must never ride a dispatch input since inputs are visible in run metadata;
- the key sourced only from a dedicated `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret, injected as a fixed `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`, with missing-secret preflight (AC 3 names `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` for the custom path too).

This PR ships only the two named providers — no `custom` option, no `provider-config` input, no `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` wiring — and the PR description does not document a descope. That is an undisclosed gap against a written acceptance criterion (and the ticket's own test matrix: "UT — custom validation" has no corresponding tests).

Two clean ways to close this:

1. **Implement AC 2a here** — add the option, the input, and the `jq`-level validation case in the resolve step (the existing `ProviderResolveStepTest` harness makes the UTs straightforward), or
2. **Descope explicitly** — carve `custom` into a follow-up card, edit it out of the ticket's AC 2a/test matrix, and state the descope in the PR description.

As shipped, the resolve step's `*)` arm makes the omission fail loudly (good), but a dispatch that selects `custom` tomorrow still requires a workflow edit — exactly what D1 exists to avoid.

It inflates the diff and blurs review focus on a PR that is otherwise tightly scoped. # gh-1471: [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

# [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Product frame

One sentence: **the terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the GLM/z.ai provider — every dispatch picks the provider (today: zai `glm-5.3-flash` or kimi-for-coding `k3-256k`), so a quota outage or a model-quality question on one provider never blocks or taints the whole benchmark programme, and cross-provider runs become directly comparable.**

Motivation (this run's scar tissue): full bench run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks (12 of them died on the FIRST request) when the z.ai GLM account quota ran out mid-run — raw 50.0% vs adjusted 60.9% on fairly-run tasks. A second provider both de-risks the quota single-point-of-failure and answers "model or harness?" by A/B running the same dataset.

## Current state (the hardcode)

- `.github/workflows/bench.yml:89` — `env.BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash` (single source of truth pin, PR #1351); shard env at `:213-215`: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: {"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"$BENCH_MODEL","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}`, key from `secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY`.
- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` (`_env`, :104-115) — passes `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` + `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` (base64) + the api key (base64) into the task container; provider plumbing is ALREADY parameterized — only the workflow hardcodes the values.
- Summary/pricing: `MODEL: $BENCH_MODEL` pins the cost column (#1339 AC3); `bench/pricing.json` has no kimi entry today (cost would render `n/a`).
- Kimi-for-coding wiring (proven in the owner's own config + the ai-teammate factory's `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path): provider type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384.

## Design

### D1 — dispatch input `provider` (choice) + `custom` escape hatch

New `workflow_dispatch` input: `provider`, `type: choice`, options `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default) / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`. A resolve step maps the choice to the full triple and FAILS HARD on an unmapped value (never a silent fallthrough to the default).

**`custom`** exists so a new provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits: a second free-text input `provider-config` carries the whole provider config as JSON — `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — passed through as `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` verbatim after validation:
- required: `baseUrl` (https:// only — plain http hard-fails), `model`; `type` optional (default `openai`-compatible);
- **the key NEVER rides the input** (dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata — a pasted key would leak): any field named like `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` hard-fails with a clear message;
- the key comes from a dedicated custom slot secret **`FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`** (rotate it per experiment), injected as a fixed `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`; missing secret + custom selected = preflight fail (D3);
- validation is `jq`-level: parse errors and schema misses fail the resolve step before any shard starts.

### D2 — dedicated bench key for kimi

New repo secret **`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`** (owner adds it in repo settings — setup blocker, see Dependencies). Mapped to the container as the config's `apiKeyEnvVar` (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH`). Deliberately NOT reusing `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`: the review factory and a multi-million-token bench must not contend for one quota (the exact failure mode this card exists to escape).

### D3 — missing-key preflight

The resolve step (or an early guard in the shard job) checks the selected provider's secret is non-empty and **fails the run in the first minute with a clear message** ("provider kimi-for-coding selected but secret FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY is not set") instead of burning 8 shards × hours on 429s. The check compares presence only — the key value is never echoed, logged, or written to artifacts (base64 passthrough stays).

### D4 — model capability fields reach the container

kimi needs `contextWindow: 200000` + `maxTokens: 16384` or the catalog/default mismatch silently truncates. Extend the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` JSON contract (and whatever consumes it — the CLI env-provider registry / fa-setup template) to carry optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`, OR pin them via the existing config path in `fa-setup.sh.j2`. Whichever lands, a zai run with NO new fields must remain byte-identical to today (REG-1).

### D5 — run identity carries provider+model

Run display name, summary header, and artifact metadata name the provider+model (e.g. `fa on terminal-bench · kimi-for-coding (k3-256k)`), so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/`/cost` views. (`name:` cannot read env contexts — resolve via the step output, same pattern as the existing comment at bench.yml:158.)

### D6 — pricing

Add a `k3-256k` entry to `bench/pricing.json`. Coding-plan pricing is subscription-based: record the per-MTok figure if published, else an explicit zero/n/a entry WITH a comment saying so — the summary must never invent a number (#1339 rule), `n/a` rendered knowingly is fine.

## Threat model / failure modes

- **Secret leak**: key only travels as env → base64 → container env; preflight prints presence, never value; session JSONL redaction (`[REDACTED:...]`) already covers the key material — verify in the kimi smoke run that the new env var name is redacted if it ever lands in a session.
- **Quota contention**: solved by D2 (dedicated key).
- **Silent default drift**: unmapped provider value = hard fail (D1); default stays zai-glm — existing scheduled/manual runs unchanged.
- **Comparability pollution**: D5 — a kimi run is unmistakable in the ledger.

## Test matrix

- **UT — resolve mapping** (`bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` family): each choice → expected (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar); unknown input → fail; missing secret env → preflight failure message names the secret.
- **UT — custom validation**: valid JSON passthrough; rejects: non-JSON, missing baseUrl/model, `http://`, fields named `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` (case-insensitive); `type` defaulting.
- **UT — config contract**: `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` with/without `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` parses; zai-shaped legacy JSON (3 fields) unchanged.
- **REG-1 (blocking)**: dispatch with NO provider input (or the default) produces a shard env identical to today's (diff the resolved env in a dry run).
- **actionlint** on the edited workflow.
- **E2E smoke (post-secret)**: manual dispatch `tasks=hello-world`, `provider=kimi-for-coding`, 1 shard → task completes, summary shows kimi model + cost column behaves, session contains no raw key.
- **E2E A/B (post-secret, optional)**: same task subset on both providers for the comparability read.

## Acceptance

1. `provider` choice input live; default = today's behavior bit-for-bit.
2. kimi-for-coding selectable; resolves to type `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k` / dedicated key env.
2a. `custom` selectable: `provider-config` JSON flows verbatim into `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`; key ONLY via `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`; raw-key-looking fields / non-https baseUrl / unparseable JSON all hard-fail preflight.
3. Missing `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi) or `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` (custom) = fast clear failure, zero shard-hours burned.
4. contextWindow/maxTokens plumbed for kimi; zai runs untouched.
5. Run identity + summary name provider/model; pricing.json entry added (number or explicit n/a).
6. Green: new UTs + REG-1 + actionlint + the hello-world kimi smoke (once the secret exists).

## Dependencies / setup

- **Owner action (blocker for E2E, not for the code)**: add repo secrets `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi-for-coding) and — when the first custom experiment arrives — `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`.
- No changes to the dmtools factory / `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path.

## Non-goals

- A provider MATRIX (same dataset on N providers in one dispatch) — separate card if wanted; this one is a single-sel…

Now let me read the remaining inputs: pr_diff.txt, pr_discussions_raw.json, ticket.json, and the CI full log. Also check if ci_failures_full.log exists (it was referenced but not in ls listing — only ci_failures.md is there). Let me check.
{"path":"input/gh-1471/pr_discussions_raw.json"}

blocks.text:
name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both). A setup-job resolve
# step maps the choice to the full provider triple and preflights the
# selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only, never a value);
# the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:` CAN read needs
# outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it (BENCH_RUN_LABEL)
# so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'

      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice

          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'

        required: false

        required: false

        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'

blocks.text:
max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="zai glm ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash' or 'kimi-for-coding'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

- run: dart pub get

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # fa-setup.sh.j2 extracts bin/fah at the top level.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux x64)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench's CLI breaks on Python 3.14 (typer: 'function' object
      # is not subscriptable).
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - run: pip install terminal-bench

      # stdlib-only unit tests for the bench scripts; a shard/patch bug
      # costs a multi-hour run, so gate shard resolution on them.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v

      # gh-1206: the shards must be sized on the SAME padded test budgets
      # the bench job writes into its dataset cache — an under-count here
      # could push a shard past the 355-min job cap.
      # Resolve the task-id list exactly like tb does (union of Path.glob
      # matches per -t pattern, against a dataset fetched via tb itself),
      # then balance shards longest-declared-budget-first (LPT, issue #142)
      # so no shard's worst case exceeds the job timeout; empty shards are
      # dropped, so a single-id smoke input degenerates to a one-job matrix.
      - name: Resolve task ids into shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR: ${{ inputs.test-timeout-floor }}
        run: |
          tb datasets download -d "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          python bench/terminal_bench/shard_tasks.py \
            --dataset-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --shards "$SHARDS" --tasks "$TASKS" \
            --test-timeout-floor "$TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR" \
            --job-cap-seconds "$((355 * 60))"
          # --job-cap-seconds takes the RAW job cap (355 min): the packer
          # subtracts its own 15-min headroom (shard_tasks.HEADROOM_SEC),
          # so the packed worst case lands at 340 min usable. Round 2 lost
          # shard-0 by ~1 min with zero headroom.

  bench:
    # gh-1471: the display name cannot read ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }} — the
    # env context is not available in job names (run 37580748776 died at
    # workflow startup on that) — but needs outputs ARE (same pattern as
    # bench-harbor.yml), so every shard names the provider+model: glm and
    # kimi runs never blend in the run history.
    name: fa on terminal-bench · ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }}
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Worst case per shard is LPT-packed to 340 min (job cap − 15 min

"""Terminal-Bench adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Follows the AbstractInstalledAgent pattern (same as the claude-code agent):
a setup script installs fa inside the task container, and the agent runs as
`fa -p "<instruction>"` in the container's tmux session, so fa's bash/read/
write tools operate on the container filesystem.

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah + lib/),
                         extracted to /opt/fa by the setup script.
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122, see bench/fa_agent_timeout.py): when any
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER is set, perform_task takes over the outer
  agent deadline from the harness's flat wait_for: the agent runs under a
  progress-aware ladder (silent => die at the base cap as today; output
  flowing => deadline recedes up to the hard ceiling). With no knobs set
  this module delegates to the stock AbstractInstalledAgent.perform_task
  byte-for-byte (historical comparability, issue #1122 REG-1).

  Round 3 (issue #1392): when FA_STALL_GAP_SEC or
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC activates the progress-watch mode, the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch (progressing trials die
  only at the absolute ceiling; a >= stall-gap gap is a provable stall).
  Every trial also gets: live per-request lines as they happen
  (LiveProgress over the pane's FA_CONN events), a per-trial
  bench_metrics.json (latency p50/p95, watchdog fires, fresh-vs-reused),
  a hang-*.json forensics dump on a stall verdict BEFORE the kill lands
  (StallSentinel), and an export-guard.json row when the agent produced
  output but the session export came back empty (ExportGuard).

  gh-1430 — the ordering invariant this adapter operates under:

      fa's watchdog is the sole arbiter of stream death; the bench gap
      only catches pane/process death.

  fa errors a truly dead provider stream itself at
  providerStreamIdleTimeout (300s, lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart)
  and, since gh-1430, heartbeats `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` to the pane
  while its stream emits events the headless output mode does not render.
  The shipped stall gap (360s = watchdog + margin, bench/fa_agent_timeout.py)
  therefore fires only when the PANE went silent — process death or a
  wedged pane — never while fa itself considers the stream live. The REG
  in test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the gap >= watchdog against the Dart
  source and fails if either side drifts.

  Issue #1406 (never-again): the launch line itself carries the
  non-secret FA_CONN_* env into the tmux pane (`export …; env |
  grep FA_CONN > /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt;` prefix — pane env belongs to the
  shell/server history, not to the step env that typed a later command),
  the capture folds into agent-logs/fa-conn-env.txt as runtime proof,
  and the loud-empty guard fires (conn-guard.json + a ::warning::
  annotation) when a trial's bench_metrics.json has requests == []
  despite real usage tokens — an instrumentation outage is never silent.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;

{"newText":"      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select(test("api.?key|^key$|token|secret"; "i"))] | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi

              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)

blocks.text:
# gh-1471: [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

# [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Product frame

One sentence: **the terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the GLM/z.ai provider — every dispatch picks the provider (today: zai `glm-5.3-flash` or kimi-for-coding `k3-256k`), so a quota outage or a model-quality question on one provider never blocks or taints the whole benchmark programme, and cross-provider runs become directly comparable.**

Motivation (this run's scar tissue): full bench run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks (12 of them died on the FIRST request) when the z.ai GLM account quota ran out mid-run — raw 50.0% vs adjusted 60.9% on fairly-run tasks. A second provider both de-risks the quota single-point-of-failure and answers "model or harness?" by A/B running the same dataset.

## Current state (the hardcode)

- `.github/workflows/bench.yml:89` — `env.BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash` (single source of truth pin, PR #1351); shard env at `:213-215`: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: {"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"$BENCH_MODEL","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}`, key from `secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY`.
- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` (`_env`, :104-115) — passes `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` + `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` (base64) + the api key (base64) into the task container; provider plumbing is ALREADY parameterized — only the workflow hardcodes the values.
- Summary/pricing: `MODEL: $BENCH_MODEL` pins the cost column (#1339 AC3); `bench/pricing.json` has no kimi entry today (cost would render `n/a`).
- Kimi-for-coding wiring (proven in the owner's own config + the ai-teammate factory's `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path): provider type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384.

## Design

### D1 — dispatch input `provider` (choice) + `custom` escape hatch

New `workflow_dispatch` input: `provider`, `type: choice`, options `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default) / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`. A resolve step maps the choice to the full triple and FAILS HARD on an unmapped value (never a silent fallthrough to the default).

**`custom`** exists so a new provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits: a second free-text input `provider-config` carries the whole provider config as JSON — `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — passed through as `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` verbatim after validation:
- required: `baseUrl` (https:// only — plain http hard-fails), `model`; `type` optional (default `openai`-compatible);
- **the key NEVER rides the input** (dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata — a pasted key would leak): any field named like `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` hard-fails with a clear message;
- the key comes from a dedicated custom slot secret **`FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`** (rotate it per experiment), injected as a fixed `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`; missing secret + custom selected = preflight fail (D3);
- validation is `jq`-level: parse errors and schema misses fail the resolve step before any shard starts.

### D2 — dedicated bench key for kimi

New repo secret **`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`** (owner adds it in repo settings — setup blocker, see Dependencies). Mapped to the container as the config's `apiKeyEnvVar` (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH`). Deliberately NOT reusing `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`: the review factory and a multi-million-token bench must not contend for one quota (the exact failure mode this card exists to escape).

### D3 — missing-key preflight

The resolve step (or an early guard in the shard job) checks the selected provider's secret is non-empty and **fails the run in the first minute with a clear message** ("provider kimi-for-coding selected but secret FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY is not set") instead of burning 8 shards × hours on 429s. The check compares presence only — the key value is never echoed, logged, or written to artifacts (base64 passthrough stays).

### D4 — model capability fields reach the container

kimi needs `contextWindow: 200000` + `maxTokens: 16384` or the catalog/default mismatch silently truncates. Extend the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` JSON contract (and whatever consumes it — the CLI env-provider registry / fa-setup template) to carry optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`, OR pin them via the existing config path in `fa-setup.sh.j2`. Whichever lands, a zai run with NO new fields must remain byte-identical to today (REG-1).

### D5 — run identity carries provider+model

Run display name, summary header, and artifact metadata name the provider+model (e.g. `fa on terminal-bench · kimi-for-coding (k3-256k)`), so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/`/cost` views. blocks.text:
name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both). A setup-job resolve
# step maps the choice to the full provider triple and preflights the
# selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only, never a value);
# the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:` CAN read needs
# outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it (BENCH_RUN_LABEL)
# so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'

max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="zai glm ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash' or 'kimi-for-coding'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

- run: dart pub get

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # fa-setup.sh.j2 extracts bin/fah at the top level.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux x64)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench's CLI breaks on Python 3.14 (typer: 'function' object
      # is not subscriptable).
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - run: pip install terminal-bench

      # stdlib-only unit tests for the bench scripts; a shard/patch bug
      # costs a multi-hour run, so gate shard resolution on them.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v

      # gh-1206: the shards must be sized on the SAME padded test budgets
      # the bench job writes into its dataset cache — an under-count here
      # could push a shard past the 355-min job cap.
      # Resolve the task-id list exactly like tb does (union of Path.glob
      # matches per -t pattern, against a dataset fetched via tb itself),
      # then balance shards longest-declared-budget-first (LPT, issue #142)
      # so no shard's worst case exceeds the job timeout; empty shards are
      # dropped, so a single-id smoke input degenerates to a one-job matrix.
      - name: Resolve task ids into shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR: ${{ inputs.test-timeout-floor }}
        run: |
          tb datasets download -d "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          python bench/terminal_bench/shard_tasks.py \
            --dataset-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --shards "$SHARDS" --tasks "$TASKS" \
            --test-timeout-floor "$TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR" \
            --job-cap-seconds "$((355 * 60))"
          # --job-cap-seconds takes the RAW job cap (355 min): the packer
          # subtracts its own 15-min headroom (shard_tasks.HEADROOM_SEC),
          # so the packed worst case lands at 340 min usable. Round 2 lost
          # shard-0 by ~1 min with zero headroom.

  bench:
    # gh-1471: the display name cannot read ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }} — the
    # env context is not available in job names (run 37580748776 died at
    # workflow startup on that) — but needs outputs ARE (same pattern as
    # bench-harbor.yml), so every shard names the provider+model: glm and
    # kimi runs never blend in the run history.
    name: fa on terminal-bench · ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }}
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Worst case per shard is LPT-packed to 340 min (job cap − 15 min
    # headroom, issue #1392); 355 min covers it under the 6 h runner cap.
    # --n-concurrent 1 keeps the math sequential-predictable and the total
    # concurrent LLM load at max-parallel x 1 (z.ai rate limits).
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Issue #1392 ShardStagger: split 8, run at most `max-concurrent`
      # (default 2) at once — GHA queues the rest and starts each the
      # moment a slot frees. This IS the concurrency experiment's
      # semaphore; no runner-side coordination.
      max-parallel: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.max-concurrent) }}
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - run: pip install terminal-bench

      # Populate tb's dataset cache, then patch it in place (tb run reuses a
      # non-empty cache without overwriting): debian:-based task images
      # cannot `apt-get update` during docker compose build since Debian
      # archived bullseye (issue #142).
      - name: Download & patch dataset
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR: ${{ inputs.test-timeout-floor }}
        run: |
          tb datasets download -d "$DATASET"
          python bench/terminal_bench/patch_dataset.py \
            "$HOME/.cache/terminal-bench/${DATASET%%==*}/${DATASET##*==}"
          # gh-1206: pad declared test budgets up to the floor so
          # slow-start verifier phases (jupyter, databases; judge phases
          # apt/pip-installing their own deps) stop dying as test_timeout
          # while the agent's work is already done. Empty/0 input = no
          # floor (declared budgets byte-for-byte).
          python bench/terminal_bench/patch_test_timeouts.py \
            "$HOME/.cache/terminal-bench/${DATASET%%==*}/${DATASET##*==}" \
            --floor "$TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR"

      - name: Run terminal-bench (fa agent)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/terminal_bench
          # gh-1471: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. Both bench keys are mapped here;
          # the run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py
          # ships exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # dataset task dir names: no whitespace, safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # Issue #1392: the forensics layer is opt-in by env — this run IS
          # the instrumented experiment, so it opts in deliberately (the
          # adapter forwards these into the container base64-encoded via
          # _CONN_ENV_KEYS). ConnTrace gives every trial's bench_metrics.json
          # its per-request/watchdog events and the [fa-bench] live lines;
          # the payload snapshot is what StallSentinel's hang-*.json
          # captures (see FA_CONN_PAYLOAD_KEEP_AUTH — the snapshot redacts
          # auth unless that is set, which bench never does).
          FA_CONN_DEBUG: '1'
          FA_CONN_TRACE_FILE: /tmp/fa-conn-trace.jsonl
          FA_CONN_PAYLOAD_SNAPSHOT: /tmp/fa-conn-snapshot.json
          # The concurrency level lands in every trial's bench_metrics.json
          # (concurrency_level) and the report's per-level latency block.
          FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY: ${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1471 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
