{"newText":"      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select(test("api.?key|^key$|token|secret"; "i"))] | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1

            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI

              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY

              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \

              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY

              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select(test("api.?key|^key$|token|secret"; "i"))] | join(", ")')

              fi

              for field in baseUrl model; do

              ;;

{"newText":"      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select(test("api.?key|^key$|token|secret"; "i"))] | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac","oldText":"      - name: Resolve provider

blocks.text:
The regex `token|secret` matches "maxTokens" — because "token" is a substring of "maxTokens"! Hmm. The intent: reject fields NAMED like key/token/secret. "maxTokens" is a legitimate capability field. I need a smarter regex: match "token" as a whole word or key-like prefix, not as part of "maxTokens". Options:

- Use word boundaries that account for camelCase: `token` should match `token`, `accessToken`, `access_token`, but NOT `maxTokens`. Tricky. `maxTokens` contains "Tokens" — case-insensitive "token" matches.

The AC says "any field named like apiKey/key/token/secret (case-insensitive)". Hmm, but "maxTokens" is a declared capability key per the ticket's own example JSON: `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — the ticket's D1 explicitly includes maxTokens in the custom config example! So maxTokens must NOT be rejected.

Regex approach: split camelCase into words and test each word. jq: `keys[] | [splits("(?=[A-Z])|_|-")] | map(select(test("^(api.?key|key|token|secret)$";"i"))) | length > 0`? Let me think: for key "maxTokens": splits on uppercase-boundary → ["max", "Tokens"] → neither equals "token" → pass. For "accessToken" → ["access","Token"] → "Token" matches `^token$` → reject. {"newText":"      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}

          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select(test("api.?key|^key$|token|secret"; "i"))] | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1

              ;;

{"newText":"      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select(test("api.?key|^key$|token|secret"; "i"))] | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac","oldText":"      - name: Resolve provider

The regex `token|secret` matches "maxTokens" — because "token" is a substring of "maxTokens"! Hmm. The intent: reject fields NAMED like key/token/secret. "maxTokens" is a legitimate capability field. I need a smarter regex: match "token" as a whole word or key-like prefix, not as part of "maxTokens". Options:

- Use word boundaries that account for camelCase: `token` should match `token`, `accessToken`, `access_token`, but NOT `maxTokens`. Tricky. `maxTokens` contains "Tokens" — case-insensitive "token" matches.

The AC says "any field named like apiKey/key/token/secret (case-insensitive)". Hmm, but "maxTokens" is a declared capability key per the ticket's own example JSON: `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — the ticket's D1 explicitly includes maxTokens in the custom config example! So maxTokens must NOT be rejected.

Regex approach: split camelCase into words and test each word. jq: `keys[] | [splits("(?=[A-Z])|_|-")] | map(select(test("^(api.?key|key|token|secret)$";"i"))) | length > 0`? Let me think: for key "maxTokens": splits on uppercase-boundary → ["max", "Tokens"] → neither equals "token" → pass. For "accessToken" → ["access","Token"] → "Token" matches `^token$` → reject. For "apiKey" → ["api","Key"]... hmm "Key" matches `^key$` → reject. Good. "APIKEY" → one word "APIKEY" → matches `^api.?key$`. Good. "api_key" → split on "_" → ["api","key"] → reject. "apikey" → "apikey" matches `^api.?key$`? "api.?key" needs "api" + any char + "key" = 7 chars; "apikey" is 6 chars. No match! Need `^api.?key$|^apikey$` or `^api_?key$`... Let me use `^(api.?key|key|token|secret)$` — "apikey" doesn't match "api.?key" (needs the middle char). So add alternation: `^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$`. Or simpler `^api_?key$` covers apikey and api_key; and "api.key"... overkill. Let me use `^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$` after splitting.

jq query:
```jq
[keys[] | select([splits("(?=[A-Z])") | select(length > 0)] | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"; "i")) | any)] | join(", ")
```

Wait, splits("(?=[A-Z])") splits before each uppercase: "maxTokens" → "max", "Tokens". "api_key" → splits only on uppercase so stays "api_key" — then test `^api.?key$` matches "api_key"? `.` matches "_" yes → "api_key" matches `^api.?key$`. And "apikey" → matches `apikey` alternation. "access_token" → one word "access_token": [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] no; `^token$` no — missed! Split on `_` and `-` too: `splits("(?=[A-Z])|_|-")`. Then "access_token" → ["access","token"] → reject. Good.

Also "userKey" → ["user","Key"] → reject. Fine — conservative is good for a security check.

But also the simple case: the existing test expects field "key" rejection and message contains the field name. The message prints the original key names — good.

Also note my test includes "api_key" — covered.

Let me rewrite the jq:

```bash
leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select([splits("(?=[A-Z])|_|-") | select(length > 0)] | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"; "i")) | any)] | join(", ")')
```

Wait — there's a subtlety: `splits` on "APIKEY" → no uppercase-boundary... "APIKEY" is all uppercase; lookahead (?=[A-Z]) matches at every position? splits with zero-width matches... `splits("(?=[A-Z])")` on "APIKEY": [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] regex matches zero-width before every uppercase letter. jq's splits handles zero-width matches by splitting at each position? That might produce empty strings — I filter `select(length > 0)`. Result would be ["A","P","I","K","E","Y"] — each single char; none matches the full-word test → "APIKEY" would PASS. Bad!

Hmm. Zero-width lookahead splitting is unreliable. Alternative approach: normalize the key by inserting separators before uppercase letters, then lowercase and split on non-alphanumerics:

```jq
keys[] | gsub("(?<![A-Z])(?=[A-Z])"; "_")  # hmm lookbehind not supported in jq (Onigmo supports it)
```

jq uses Onigmo regex which supports lookbehind. Let me try a simpler approach: transform then test:

```jq
def words: gsub("([a-z0-9])([A-Z])"; "\1_\2") | gsub("[-_]"; ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
[keys[] | select(. | words | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$")) | any)] | join(", ")
```

"apiKey" → "api_Key" → "api key" → ["api","key"] → key matches. Good.
"maxTokens" → "max_Tokens" → ["max","tokens"] → no match. Good.
"accessToken" → ["access","token"] → reject. Good.
"access_token" → "access token" → reject. Good.
"Key" → "key" → reject. Good.
"SECRET" → "secret" → reject. Good.

But careful: the first gsub on "maxTokens" → "max_Tokens"; second → "max Tokens" → split ["max","tokens"]. Good.

name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # Issue #1234 rework: 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override (a
      # gates.loc.sources key is a ConfigException — caught here on

{"newText":"      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '[keys[] | select(test("api.?key|^key$|token|secret"; "i"))] | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac","oldText":"      - name: Resolve provider

The regex `token|secret` matches "maxTokens" — because "token" is a substring of "maxTokens"! Hmm. The intent: reject fields NAMED like key/token/secret. "maxTokens" is a legitimate capability field. I need a smarter regex: match "token" as a whole word or key-like prefix, not as part of "maxTokens". Options:

- Use word boundaries that account for camelCase: `token` should match `token`, `accessToken`, `access_token`, but NOT `maxTokens`. Tricky. `maxTokens` contains "Tokens" — case-insensitive "token" matches.

The AC says "any field named like apiKey/key/token/secret (case-insensitive)". Hmm, but "maxTokens" is a declared capability key per the ticket's own example JSON: `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — the ticket's D1 explicitly includes maxTokens in the custom config example! So maxTokens must NOT be rejected.

Regex approach: split camelCase into words and test each word. jq: `keys[] | [splits("(?=[A-Z])|_|-")] | map(select(test("^(api.?key|key|token|secret)$";"i"))) | length > 0`? Let me think: for key "maxTokens": splits on uppercase-boundary → ["max", "Tokens"] → neither equals "token" → pass. For "accessToken" → ["access","Token"] → "Token" matches `^token$` → reject. For "apiKey" → ["api","Key"]... hmm "Key" matches `^key$` → reject. Good. "APIKEY" → one word "APIKEY" → matches `^api.?key$`. Good. "api_key" → split on "_" → ["api","key"] → reject. "apikey" → "apikey" matches `^api.?key$`? "api.?key" needs "api" + any char + "key" = 7 chars; "apikey" is 6 chars. No match! Need `^api.?key$|^apikey$` or `^api_?key$`... Let me use `^(api.?key|key|token|secret)$` — "apikey" doesn't match "api.?key" (needs the middle char). So add alternation: `^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$`. Or simpler `^api_?key$` covers apikey and api_key; and "api.key"... overkill. Let me use `^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$` after splitting.

jq query:
```jq
[keys[] | select([splits("(?=[A-Z])") | select(length > 0)] | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"; "i")) | any)] | join(", ")
```

Wait, splits("(?=[A-Z])") splits before each uppercase: "maxTokens" → "max", "Tokens". "api_key" → splits only on uppercase so stays "api_key" — then test `^api.?key$` matches "api_key"? `.` matches "_" yes → "api_key" matches `^api.?key$`. And "apikey" → matches `apikey` alternation. The regex `token|secret` matches "maxTokens" — because "token" is a substring of "maxTokens"! Hmm. The intent: reject fields NAMED like key/token/secret. "maxTokens" is a legitimate capability field. I need a smarter regex: match "token" as a whole word or key-like prefix, not as part of "maxTokens". Options:

- Use word boundaries that account for camelCase: `token` should match `token`, `accessToken`, `access_token`, but NOT `maxTokens`. Tricky. `maxTokens` contains "Tokens" — case-insensitive "token" matches.

The AC says "any field named like apiKey/key/token/secret (case-insensitive)". Hmm, but "maxTokens" is a declared capability key per the ticket's own example JSON: `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — the ticket's D1 explicitly includes maxTokens in the custom config example! So maxTokens must NOT be rejected.

Regex approach: split camelCase into words and test each word. jq: `keys[] | [splits("(?=[A-Z])|_|-")] | map(select(test("^(api.?key|key|token|secret)$";"i"))) | length > 0`? Let me think: for key "maxTokens": splits on uppercase-boundary → ["max", "Tokens"] → neither equals "token" → pass. For "accessToken" → ["access","Token"] → "Token" matches `^token$` → reject. For "apiKey" → ["api","Key"]... hmm "Key" matches `^key$` → reject. Good. "APIKEY" → one word "APIKEY" → matches `^api.?key$`. Good. "api_key" → split on "_" → ["api","key"] → reject. "apikey" → "apikey" matches `^api.?key$`? "api.?key" needs "api" + any char + "key" = 7 chars; "apikey" is 6 chars. No match! Need `^api.?key$|^apikey$` or `^api_?key$`... Let me use `^(api.?key|key|token|secret)$` — "apikey" doesn't match "api.?key" (needs the middle char). So add alternation: `^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$`. Or simpler `^api_?key$` covers apikey and api_key; and "api.key"... overkill. Let me use `^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$` after splitting.

jq query:
```jq
[keys[] | select([splits("(?=[A-Z])") | select(length > 0)] | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"; "i")) | any)] | join(", ")
```

Wait, splits("(?=[A-Z])") splits before each uppercase: "maxTokens" → "max", "Tokens". "api_key" → splits only on uppercase so stays "api_key" — then test `^api.?key$` matches "api_key"? `.` matches "_" yes → "api_key" matches `^api.?key$`. And "apikey" → matches `apikey` alternation. "access_token" → one word "access_token": [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] no; `^token$` no — missed! Split on `_` and `-` too: `splits("(?=[A-Z])|_|-")`. Then "access_token" → ["access","token"] → reject. Good.

Also "userKey" → ["user","Key"] → reject. Fine — conservative is good for a security check.

Also note my test includes "api_key" — covered.

```

Wait — there's a subtlety: `splits` on "APIKEY" → no uppercase-boundary... "APIKEY" is all uppercase; lookahead (?=[A-Z]) matches at every position? splits with zero-width matches... `splits("(?=[A-Z])")` on "APIKEY": [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] regex matches zero-width before every uppercase letter. jq's splits handles zero-width matches by splitting at each position? That might produce empty strings — I filter `select(length > 0)`. Result would be ["A","P","I","K","E","Y"] — each single char; none matches the full-word test → "APIKEY" would PASS. Bad!

Hmm. Zero-width lookahead splitting is unreliable. Alternative approach: normalize the key by inserting separators before uppercase letters, then lowercase and split on non-alphanumerics:

blocks.text:
jq's string literal doesn't support `\1` escapes (that's only in the regex replacement via capture interpolation? Actually jq replacement strings support `\(.capture)` named interpolation only in newer versions via `gsub(re; str)` where str can use `\(...)`? No — jq replacement supports named captures `(?<x>...)` interpolated as `\(.x)`? Hmm. In jq, `gsub("(?<a>[a-z])(?<b>[A-Z])"; "\(.a)_\(.b)")` — named capture groups can be interpolated with `\(.name)`. Backreferences `\1` are not supported.

Use named captures:
```
gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
```

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

Actually jq replacement strings support `\(.capture)` named interpolation only in newer versions via `gsub(re; str)` where str can use `\(...)`? No — jq replacement supports named captures `(?<x>...)` interpolated as `\(.x)`? Hmm. In jq, `gsub("(?<a>[a-z])(?<b>[A-Z])"; "\(.a)_\(.b)")` — named capture groups can be interpolated with `\(.name)`. Backreferences `\1` are not supported.

Use named captures:
```
gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")

BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

blocks.text:
One security check: in the "not a JSON object" error, `$PROVIDER_CONFIG` is echoed — could that leak a key? If it's unparseable it can't contain a structured key... it could literally be `{"apiKey":"[REDACTED:credential]"` malformed. Echoing raw input to the log could leak a pasted key! Hmm. But wait — the object check runs BEFORE the key-field scan, so a malformed JSON containing a key value would be echoed. Better to not echo the raw config. Also the baseUrl echo: baseUrl itself was validated as a string; echoing it is fine (it's a URL, not key material — and the key-field scan already passed, though a key could hide in a non-key-named field... the AC only requires rejecting key-NAMED fields; values of arbitrary fields could contain anything, but echoing just baseUrl is minimal).

Let me remove the raw `$PROVIDER_CONFIG` from the object-check error message to be safe. The test `test_custom_rejects_non_json` asserts "provider-config" in message — fine. `test_custom_rejects_non_object_json` doesn't check message content. Also the empty-input message is fine.

Also `provider custom selected but secret FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY is not set` — from the shared preflight, names provider ($PROVIDER="custom") and secret. Good.

One more: `model` from jq -r '.model' — if model is a non-string JSON (e.g. number), the earlier required-field check demands `type == "string" and length > 0` for model — so by this point model is a non-empty string. Good. Same for baseUrl.

              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact

              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '

                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')

BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
