          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

{"content":"# Rework: gh-1471 review threads + CI failures

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **AC 2a implemented** (was the blocking gap): the `custom` provider
  escape hatch is now a dispatch choice — `provider-config` free-text
  input, `jq`-level validation in the resolve step, key sourced only
  from `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` and injected as the fixed
  `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`. See **Approach** below.
- ❌ **CI failures fixed** — both red checks had one root cause:
  `CRAP + duplication` failed on `(top-level)._parseConfig`
  (`lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart`) at **CRAP 13.00 > 12.00**
  (new code from this PR, 100% covered — pure complexity), and the
  `Quality gate` failure was the same `guards` leg propagating
  (`R_GUARDS: failure`). `_parseConfig` is split (per-entry routing →
  `_takeConfigEntry` + `_ParsedConfig` accumulator); verified locally
  with the pinned `crap4dart 0.11.0` + lcov: file max CRAP is now
  **10.00** at 100% coverage, threshold 12.
- 💡 Run-identity spelling unified (suggestion 2) and the `fa_agent.py`
  docstring note from the automated review is addressed. The dartfmt
  churn suggestion (3) is answered with evidence in its thread reply —
  the hunks are the repo SDK's canonical `dart format` output over
  `origin/main` content, so reverting would re-dirty the tree (the
  pre-commit self-heal would re-wrap on the next staged commit).
- The machine verdict-record thread (`dmtools:review-verdict`, gh-807)
  says "Do not edit or reply" — no reply posted for it; this comment
  carries the human-readable resolution.

## Approach

### 1. AC 2a — the `custom` provider escape hatch (blocking)

`.github/workflows/bench.yml`:

- `provider` choice gains the `custom` option; new `provider-config`
  free-text dispatch input (default `''`) carries the provider JSON.
- The resolve step's `custom` arm validates with `jq` **before any shard
  starts**, each failure naming the offending input:
  1. must parse as a JSON object (the raw input is **not** echoed — a
     malformed payload could smuggle key material into the log);
  2. **key-like fields hard-fail**: whole-word match on each key's
     split words (camelCase/snake_case divided, case-insensitive) against
     `api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret` — so the legitimate `maxTokens`
     capability key passes while `apiKey`/`APIKEY`/`key`/`token`/
     `accessToken`/`api_key`/`SECRET` are all caught (first cut used a
     substring regex and false-positived on `maxTokens`; fixed);
  3. required non-empty string `baseUrl` **and** `model`;
  4. `baseUrl` must start with `https://` (plain http would put the
     bench key on a cleartext wire);
  5. passthrough: every declared field rides `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`
     verbatim (via `jq -c`) plus the fixed `{apiKeyEnvVar:
     "FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM"}` injection; `type` defaults to `openai`
     (openai-compatible catalog entry).
- The key comes **only** from `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`: the shared preflight
  (`secret_value` check) names it, missing secret fails in minute one;
  `::add-mask::` covers the base64 transport form like the other keys.
- The shard step maps `FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}`;
  the run block's existing `${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}` indirection picks it
  by name — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing.
- Run identity for a custom run: job name / summary header show
  `custom (<model>)` via the same `run_label` output.

### 2. Run-identity spelling (suggestion 2)

The zai arm's `run_label` now derives from the dispatch choice id
(`zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)`) instead of the ad-hoc
`zai glm (...)` — one spelling on `run-name`, shard job names, and the
summary `Provider:` header (kimi already matched its choice id). REG-1 is
untouched: `provider_config` for the default stays byte-identical to the
pre-gh-1471 3-field zai JSON (pinned by UT).

### 3. CI CRAP fix (root cause of both red checks)

`lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart`: `_parseConfig` carried all
per-entry branches (complexity 13). Extracted `_takeConfigEntry` (key
routing into a `_ParsedConfig` accumulator) — `_parseConfig` keeps only
the shape checks. No behavior change; all existing named-error messages
preserved.

### 4. Review polish

- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` module docstring now documents the
  optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` pair of `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`
  (gh-1471 D4).
- Suggestion 3 (dartfmt churn) answered in the thread reply with
  reproducible evidence rather than reverted — see
  `outputs/review_replies/thread_3.md`.

## Files Modified

- `.github/workflows/bench.yml` — `custom` option + `provider-config`
  input; resolve-step `custom` arm with jq validation;
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` wiring in resolve env + shard env; zai
  `run_label` from the choice id; header comment updated.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` — `_run_resolve` extended
  (`PROVIDER_CONFIG`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`); 9 new custom-path UTs
  (verbatim passthrough, type defaulting, non-JSON / non-object /
  missing-field / http / key-like-case-insensitive rejections, missing
  custom secret, key-never-in-log); zai `run_label` pin updated; shape
  tests for the new input/option/secret mappings.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py` — the env-label test's zai
  label pin updated to the unified spelling.
- `lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart` — CRAP refactor only
  (`_parseConfig` → `_takeConfigEntry` + `_ParsedConfig`).
- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` — docstring: optional
  `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` documented.

## Test Coverage

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` — **336 tests
  OK** (15 skipped, pre-existing skips), incl. the new
  `ProviderResolveStepTest` custom-validation cases (328 → 336).

custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi

BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then

              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.

                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")

              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k

                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')

                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi

One security check: in the "not a JSON object" error, `$PROVIDER_CONFIG` is echoed — could that leak a key? If it's unparseable it can't contain a structured key... it could literally be `{"apiKey":"[REDACTED:credential]"` malformed. Echoing raw input to the log could leak a pasted key! Hmm. But wait — the object check runs BEFORE the key-field scan, so a malformed JSON containing a key value would be echoed. Better to not echo the raw config. custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi

              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'

              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1

                [keys[]

                      | any)]

                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi

              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1

              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1

              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;

          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then

custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi

              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1

custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi

            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi

              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY

              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then

              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do

              done

              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')

              ;;

              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;

### 1. AC 2a — the `custom` provider escape hatch (blocking)

`.github/workflows/bench.yml`:

- `provider` choice gains the `custom` option; new `provider-config`

custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi

BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — got: $PROVIDER_CONFIG"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

One security check: in the "not a JSON object" error, `$PROVIDER_CONFIG` is echoed — could that leak a key? If it's unparseable it can't contain a structured key... it could literally be `{"apiKey":"[REDACTED:credential]"` malformed. Echoing raw input to the log could leak a pasted key! Hmm. But wait — the object check runs BEFORE the key-field scan, so a malformed JSON containing a key value would be echoed. Better to not echo the raw config. Also the baseUrl echo: baseUrl itself was validated as a string; echoing it is fine (it's a URL, not key material — and the key-field scan already passed, though a key could hide in a non-key-named field... the AC only requires rejecting key-NAMED fields; values of arbitrary fields could contain anything, but echoing just baseUrl is minimal).

Let me remove the raw `$PROVIDER_CONFIG` from the object-check error message to be safe. The test `test_custom_rejects_non_json` asserts "provider-config" in message — fine. `test_custom_rejects_non_object_json` doesn't check message content. Also the empty-input message is fine.

Also `provider custom selected but secret FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY is not set` — from the shared preflight, names provider ($PROVIDER="custom") and secret. Good.

One more: `model` from jq -r '.model' — if model is a non-string JSON (e.g. number), the earlier required-field check demands `type == "string" and length > 0` for model — so by this point model is a non-empty string. Good. Same for baseUrl.
